newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says to tell DKB to improve management.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says to tell DKB to improve management.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) plans to instruct Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd to strengthen management of its business, including risk management, to prevent incidents such as loans to racketeers from recurring, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Thursday.
He said he would instruct DKB to do so after receiving a final report from the bank on loans it made to a corporate racketeer.
Matsushita said DKB failed during a BOJ inspection in August 1991 to disclose loans made to a client thought to be linked to a racketeer.
This was revealed in a recent report by DKB to the central bank, he said.
But the recent report failed to explain why DKB made such loans or to explain details of business management within the bank.
So the BOJ had asked DKB to explain the reasons for making such loans, Matsushita said.

On receiving a final report from DKB, Matsushita said: "We would like to instruct the bank to strengthen risk management and overall business management in order to prevent such things from happening again."
